notes.meaning: Noah's three sons began having children after the great flood washed the old world away. This family record traces how their descendants started to refill the earth just as God had commanded them. It marks a fresh start for human history through these three brothers.

Japheth's family is listed first, naming seven sons who moved into the regions of modern Turkey and Europe. Over time, their descendants became groups like the Medes, Greeks, and other northern peoples. God guided their steps as they settled in new lands far from Babel.

Gomer's three sons settled in the regions north and east of the Black Sea and near Armenia. Later, these family lines grew into large tribes that lived in rugged northern mountains. Their settlements show how quickly Japheth's descendants moved into new territories.

Javan's sons gave rise to coastal and island peoples around the Mediterranean Sea. Places like Greece, Cyprus, and Rhodes trace their earliest settlements back to these family groups. They helped open early trade routes across the waters.

Japheth's descendants became seafaring peoples who spread across various coasts and islands. Each group developed its own lands, clans, and distinct spoken languages over time. This verse looks ahead to the way nations separated after the tower of Babel.

Ham's four sons headed mostly southward into Africa and parts of the Near East. Mizraim is the Hebrew name for Egypt, Cush settled around Ethiopia and southern regions, Put lived near Libya, and Canaan took the land along the Jordan River. Many of these nations became close, troublesome neighbors to Israel.

The sons and grandsons of Cush settled along the coasts and trading routes of the Arabian peninsula. Among them were Sheba and Dedan, who became famous in Bible times as wealthy merchants. God placed these tribes along key desert highways.

Cush also fathered Nimrod, who broke away from ordinary clan life to become a mighty warrior and ruler on earth. Before him, men lived as equal neighbors under family leaders. Nimrod used his strength and ambition to build the world's very first kingdom.

Nimrod became famous for hunting down dangerous wild beasts to protect early settlements. His great hunting skill won people over and allowed him to gather men under his command. He grew so famous that people used his name as a common proverb for strength.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Latin church writers such as Augustine viewed Nimrod as an arrogant rebel who hunted and oppressed men in open defiance against God.

notes.meaning: Nimrod's empire began in the southern plains of Mesopotamia, known as the land of Shinar. He brought several major cities under his rule, including Babel, Erech, and Akkad. This marked the start of the Babylonian empire, which would later play a large role in Israel's history.

Nimrod pushed his conquests northward into Assyria and built cities like Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah, and Resen. Resen was built between Nineveh and Calah, helping to form a vast network of cities. These centers grew into the mighty Assyrian empire that later troubled God's people.

Mizraim, the father of Egypt, had many family branches that settled throughout northern and southern Egypt as well as parts of North Africa. One of these branches gave rise to the Philistines, who originally came from Crete and the Mediterranean coast. The Philistines would later become constant rivals of Israel.

Canaan's family line began with his firstborn son, Sidon, who founded the famous northern trading city. His descendants also included tribal groups like the Hittites, Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites. These nations were the very peoples Israel later encountered in the land.

This list finishes naming the rest of the Canaanite tribes, including the Hivites and several coastal peoples of Phoenicia. Over time, these clans spread across the valleys, hills, and shoreline of the region. Their growing numbers showed how God allowed even fallen nations to multiply.

The writer traces the borders of Canaan from Sidon in the north down toward Gaza, and east toward Sodom and Gomorrah. The Bible gives these exact borders because God later gave this land to Abraham and his descendants. It shows that God was already preparing a home for His chosen nation.

This statement wraps up the family tree of Ham's sons and grandsons. It groups them by their clans, languages, territories, and nations across Africa and the Near East. God knew every tribe and kept track of where they lived.

Shem is introduced with special respect as the older brother of Japheth and the ancestor of Eber. The word Hebrew comes from Eber's name, pointing directly to Abraham and the people of Israel. Shem receives this place of honor because the promised Savior would be born from his line.

Shem's five sons lived in the lands east and northeast of Canaan, including Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. These lines became major nations like the Persians, Assyrians, and Syrians. God placed these Semitic families across the heart of ancient Mesopotamia.

Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash, whose families settled across Syria and the plains near Mesopotamia. Job came from the land named after Uz. These tribes lived mainly in open country and along desert borders.

The family line leading to Abraham continues from Arphaxad to Shelah, and then to Eber. Eber is singled out because his name is the root of the word Hebrew, marking God's chosen people. Through these quiet generations, God was steadily protecting the family of promise.

Eber named his first son Peleg, which means division, because the people of the earth were divided into separate nations during his lifetime. This name looked back to God confusing the languages at the Tower of Babel. Eber's other son, Joktan, became the father of many large Arab tribes.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that the division in Peleg's day was a physical splitting apart of the earth's continents, rather than the division of languages and people at Babel.

notes.meaning: Joktan fathered many sons who became the heads of tribes in southern Arabia. Hazarmaveth gave his name to a region famous for spices and incense, while Uzal was an ancient capital city in Yemen. These verses record real families who settled the Arabian deserts.

Joktan had thirteen sons in all, including Sheba and Ophir. Sheba formed a famous merchant kingdom, while Ophir became well known in later Bible history for its pure gold. God blessed these distant families with wealth and wide trade.

The land of Joktan's descendants stretched from Mesha all the way to Sephar in the eastern mountains of Arabia. They lived a pastoral life moving herds across the rugged, hilly country. God fixed their home in that distant desert corner of the world.

This verse concludes the record of Shem's family, summarizing his descendants by their clans, languages, territories, and nations. Though they grew into different peoples speaking different tongues, they all shared Shem as their ancestor. God guided each branch into its appointed land.

This final summary looks back across the seventy nations that came from Noah's three sons after the flood. It reminds us that every nation on earth belongs to one single human family made by God. God spread these peoples abroad so that the whole earth would be filled with life again.
